sections.html:
Meriwether County is a rural county in west central Georgia, counted inside the Atlanta metro area, with Greenville as the county seat and Manchester as its largest city. Greenville, Luthersville, Manchester, Warm Springs and Woodbury are cities. Gay, Lone Oak and Pine Mountain are towns, and Alvaton is unincorporated. A lot inside Manchester and a farm on a county road land on one county bill, while a lot in the Town of Gay adds a separate city bill.

Owners occupy 73.0% of homes, and the typical owner-occupied house is valued at $168,800. Median gross rent is $920. The county had an estimated 21,516 residents in July 2025, up 4.4% from the 20,613 counted in 2020, and it has 10,478 housing units across 8,391 households. Builders took out 117 permits in 2025. Median household income is $57,340 and the average drive to work takes 34.3 minutes, so buyers here watch carrying costs closely, and a parcel with a clean tax record is easier to sell.

sections.h2: Who sends and collects the bill
sections.html:
Billing and collection happen at the tax commissioner's counter, 17234 Roosevelt Highway, Building A, Greenville. Call (706) 672-4219. The doors are open Monday to Friday from 8:30 to 4:30, and letters go to PO Box 729, Greenville, GA 30222.

The Board of Tax Assessors (706 672-4222) appraises. Disputes over its numbers reach a Board of Equalization staffed by grand jury appointees. The county commission and the school board vote on separate millage rates, where a mill means $1 of tax on every $1,000 assessed.

Residents of Luthersville, Manchester, Warm Springs, Woodbury, Greenville and Lone Oak pay city and county tax together to the county commissioner. The Town of Gay collects its own city tax, so a Gay owner pays the county here and the town separately. The tax site also has tabs for tax sales and excess funds.

Land, houses and business personal property owe their tax to Meriwether County by December 20. Bills normally go in the mail by October 1. If yours has not arrived by October 15, call the office.

Meriwether County property tax due dates
Property typeDue date
Land, houses and business equipmentDecember 20
Mobile homesApril 1, with the decal posted by that date
BoatsNovember 15, after May assessment notices and a 45 day appeal window
Boat, equipment and other personal property billsMailed at least 60 days ahead, usually in mid November
Cars and trucksRenewal follows the owner's birth date

State rules let a county shift its official date to December 1 or November 15, or split the bill into installments, and interest waits until 60 days after the bill is postmarked. The printed bill is what you answer to.

Late real estate bills collect interest starting the day after December 20, then a penalty that builds in steps. The interest rate on real and personal property is reset yearly, so ask the counter for the rate in force.

  • Real and personal property: 5% lands on the 120th day past due, and again every 120 days, with a ceiling of 20%.
  • Mobile homes: one flat 10% penalty, with 1% interest.
  • Lien: a FiFa is filed with the Clerk of Superior Court once a bill is 90 days overdue, and credit bureaus can read it.

The counter takes partial payments while interest keeps running. Paying off a recorded lien before listing keeps it out of the buyer's title search.

Payments can arrive at the counter, on the website, by mail or in the drop box out front. Inside, the staff take checks, cash and cards (Visa, MasterCard and Discover), and the website takes cards or PayPal.

  • Website card payments add a fee of 2.57%, with a $1.50 floor.
  • Cards run at the counter or by phone add 3.00%, again with a $1.50 floor.
  • Mail a check to the Meriwether County Tax Commissioner at the PO Box above and write the parcel number on it.

Homeowners with an escrow account can ask the office to share tax data with the lender, or mail the coupons to the lender with a short note.

Notices usually mail in the spring, and the written appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors first, naming the route you pick.

You may argue taxability, worth, fairness against similar parcels, or a refused exemption. A Board of Equalization or an arbitrator hears the case, and the state also provides a hearing officer. Any route can end in superior court. Keep a few recent nearby sales and photos of any condition problems with the file, since specifics carry more weight than general complaints.

Homestead is the biggest one. Live in the house on January 1, file before April 1, and it applies that year.

First-time owners should bring a warranty deed, and the driver's license must show the Meriwether County street address, because a post office box is not accepted. An additional exemption begins at age 62. Business owners can ask about the freeport exemption on inventory, and the assessors make the final call on eligibility. Ask the Tax Assessor's office about conservation use or other special programs.

Manufactured homes, boats and heavy equipment each follow their own rules at the Greenville counter. Every mobile home must show a current decal by April 1, and decals are issued once tax is paid: on the spot for walk-in payers, by mail for everyone else.

Anyone placing a mobile home in the county should visit the Building and Zoning office next door to the commissioner, which takes appointments at 706-672-1283. A buyer or new owner has 30 days to apply for a title and must bring a paid tax receipt and proof of ownership.

Boats need Department of Natural Resources registration and are taxed on value. Tractors, farm equipment and machinery also count as personal property. Heavy equipment bought from a dealer is taxed in the purchase year, with a return due at the commissioner's office 30 days after that month ends. Timber harvests are reported on Department of Revenue form PT-283T, available from the assessors at (706) 672-4222. Deeds sit in the courthouse deed room run by the Clerk of Superior Court, so ask there for a copy of yours.

The January 1 titleholder owes the whole year, with no refund for part of it. Put any buyer and seller split in the contract.

  1. A few days before closing, request a written balance from the tax commissioner that shows penalties and any lien.
  2. Pay back taxes out of your payoff at the table.
  3. If the sale closes before the fall bills mail, ask the closing attorney how that year's bill is being handled.

A cash buyer will still ask for a clear tax record, so a recorded lien is worth paying off before you list.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Meriwether County tax office?
faqs.a: Dial (706) 672-4219 for billing and payments. Value questions go to (706) 672-4222.

faqs.q: When does Meriwether County want its real estate tax?
faqs.a: December 20. Bills normally mail by October 1, and anyone still waiting on October 15 should call.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Meriwether County bill online?
faqs.a: Yes, by card or PayPal on meriwethertax.com, with a 2.57% fee that has a $1.50 floor. The counter, the mail and the front drop box also work.

faqs.q: If I sell in Meriwether County, is that year's tax erased?
faqs.a: No. The January 1 owner stays liable for the year and Georgia gives no refund for part of one, so put the split in the sales contract.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to fight a Meriwether County value?
faqs.a: Counting from the notice date, you get 45 days. The written appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors and names either the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.
